tools.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

{"number":16860,"title":"feat(skills): replace the all-on skill catalog with an explicit allow-list","body":"HUMAN:

Enable a set of reccomanded skills as default and not the whole package. 

AGENT:

Phases 1 and 2 of the plan in #16302. Phase 0 (the `defaultEnabled` catalog flag and `DEFAULT_ENABLED_SKILL_NAMES`) shipped in OpenHands/extensions#485 and is already on `@openhands/extensions@0.18.0`, which this repo pins.

Evidence below is a real run of the Customize page against the change, not just unit tests: 59 catalog skills render, 11 on, 48 off, and `add-javadoc` — the skill from the issue report — is among the 48.

---

## Why

Nothing is installed today. The whole `@openhands/extensions` catalog is baked into the bundle at build time and merged into `agent_context.skills` for every conversation, with `disabled_skills` as the only escape hatch. All-on-with-a-deny-list means every catalog addition is on by default for everyone, which is how @rbren ended up opted into javadoc and bitbucket skills. The cost isn't disk — it's ~60 skill bodies and 60 trigger sets competing in every system prompt.

## Summary

- `enabled_skills`: an allow-list **over the bundled catalog only**, defaulting to the 11 entries the catalog flags `defaultEnabled`. `disabled_skills` keeps its job for user- and project-authored skills, which are discovered at runtime from `.agents/skills/` and should be on the moment they appear. `src/utils/skill-enablement.ts` is the single place that decides which list a skill belongs to.
- A one-shot migration at the app root (`useMigrateEnabledSkills`): a workspace whose deny-list names a catalog skill keeps everything else on (behaviour preserved); a fresh one gets the curated default; one that already has `enabled_skills` is untouched. Both branches persist an **explicit** list, which is what stops a later `defaultEnabled` addition from switching itself on. `undefined` is the "never migrated" sentinel, so it is deliberately kept out of `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` and out of the `use-settings` coercions.
- A skill the opening message invokes by name (`/standup-digest:setup`, or `/<skill-name>` from the "Use skill" button) is loaded for that conversation whatever the lists say. Automation preset cards fill the input with exactly that command, and 18 of the catalog's 24 slash commands belong to skills that are off by default — without this the card would silently do nothing. Only the leading token counts.
- Customize gets a "Recommended" badge and a matching facet; the Customize page and the conversation drawer, which each carried their own copy of the hydrate/auto-save/toggle logic, now share `useSkillEnablement` so one surface can't write a preference the other can't see.

## Issue Number

Fixes #16302

## How to Test

```
npm ci
VITE_FRONTEND_PORT=5199 npm run dev:mock
# open http://localhost:5199/skills
```

Expect 59 skill cards with 11 enabled and 48 disabled, a `RECOMMENDATION` facet next to `STATE`, "Recommended" pills on the 11, and the notice under the page description. `add-javadoc` and the `bitbucket*` skills — the ones reported in #16302 — start off; toggling one on writes `enabled_skills`, not `disabled_skills` (visible in the PATCH `misc_settings_diff.app_preferences`).

For the migration: seed `disabled_skills` with a catalog name before first load and confirm the persisted `enabled_skills` is the whole catalog minus that name, not the curated default.

Automated:

- `npx vitest run` → 5064 passed. One unrelated pre-existing failure, `dev-with-automation` SIGHUP cleanup, which fails the same way on an untouched `main`.
- `npm run lint` and `npm run check-translation-completeness` clean; the 4 new keys are translated for all 15 locales.
- New: `__tests__/utils/skill-enablement.test.ts` (resolve / deny-veto / every migration branch), `__tests__/hooks/use-migrate-enabled-skills.test.tsx` (one-shot, cloud skip, no write over a failed settings load), plus route and facet cases.
- The two adapter tests that asserted `add-javadoc` reaches the agent context now assert the opposite — that flip **is** the fix.

## Video/Screenshots

Customize → Skills, default state after the change. `STATE` reads Enabled 11 / Disabled 48; `add-javadoc` and `agent-creator` are off, `add-skill` / `agent-canvas-environment` / `agent-memory` are on and badged:

![Skills page, 11 of 59 enabled by default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/e5c848586bed65324d126314691f661e185b5139/.github/pr-assets/pr-16860-01-skills-default.png)

The new `RECOMMENDATION` facet, narrowed to Recommended — 11 results, all enabled:

![Recommendation facet filtered to Recommended](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/e5c848586bed65324d126314691f661e185b5139/.github/pr-assets/pr-16860-02-recommended-facet.png)

## Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Docs / chore

## Notes

Deviations from the plan in the issue, worth a look at review:

- **No `Core` tier.** The shaped spec asked for mutually exclusive `Core` / `Recommended` tags, which forces `core` to secretly mean "core **and** default-on". Grepping every catalog name against `src/` (minus i18n), exactly one skill is referenced by Canvas code — `add-skill`, via `/add-skill` and the restart banner — and disabling it degrades that flow rather than breaking Canvas. So: one flag, no locked toggles. If something genuinely unremovable appears later, the lock is a Canvas-side const and a union in one resolver.
- **The deny-list still wins over the allow-list.** Only matters before the migration lands: until then a pre-existing "I turned this off" lives in `disabled_skills` alone, and the allow-list fallback would otherwise switch it back on. Post-migration the two lists are disjoint and the clause is a no-op.
- **A shared hook, rather than only touching `skills-settings.tsx`** as the plan said. `conversation-overview-skills-panel.tsx` runs the same logic; leaving it on the deny-list would have made its catalog toggles silently no-op.
- **Cloud is untouched**, per the plan: it creates conversations from its own server-side catalog and never reads `agent_context`, so both the migration and the allow-list UI are gated to local. Cloud keeps today's deny-list behaviour.
- **Install/download is out of scope** and the spec's "Installation and updates" section doesn't apply: catalog skills are bundled, never downloaded, so there is no enable-time install, no uninstall, and neither failure mode exists. (Real install/uninstall exists for a different system — git-sourced plugins in `plugins-management-service.ts`.)

One unrelated, pre-existing test is flaky across both E2E suites: `mock-llm-automation.spec.ts:376 › step 2: create automation and dispatch run via the UI` ("Created automation ID was not reported after 30000ms", Playwright exit 124). It fails identically on `main` — [run 32388224354](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/actions/runs/32388224354), 2026-08-20, before this branch existed — and it alternates between the two suites run to run: `mock-llm-docker-e2e` green and `mock-llm-e2e` red on one commit, the reverse on the next. It uses a plain-English prompt against `openhands-automation`, which is default-enabled, so the allow-list does not touch it.

Both suites have since gone green at least once on this branch, and the `preset automation → slash command conversation › direct slash command from home page triggers skill activation` spec — the one this change actually broke — has passed in every run since the fix.

The first CI run caught a real regression this way: the mock-LLM E2E `preset automation → slash command conversation` spec came back with `activated_skills=[]`, which is what surfaced the automation-card dependency on catalog skills. Fixed in `fix(skills): load a catalog skill the opening slash command invokes`.

Follow-ups, phase 3 in the plan, each its own issue:

- Per-workspace scoping — needs a metadata bag on `LocalWorkspace`, which is an SDK `WorkspacesClient` schema change first. Phases 1–2 are app-global and fix the reported problem.
- Cloud parity — the cloud catalog and conversation-create path need their own filtering.
- The agent-profile `disabled_skills` deny-list is a second, independent list the adapter never consults; which one wins is unresolved.

[{"sha":"b28af79ef06f6aedb449b56888ebe9b727c48939","message":"feat(skills): allow-list bundled catalog skills instead of shipping all of them

Every skill in the `@openhands/extensions` catalog is baked into the bundle at
build time and merged into `agent_context.skills` for every conversation, with
`disabled_skills` as the only way out. That deny-list means each catalog
addition is on by default for everyone — the reported symptom in #16302, where
a user found themselves opted into javadoc and bitbucket skills. The cost is
not disk but ~60 skill bodies and trigger sets competing in every system
prompt.

Introduce `enabled_skills`, an allow-list over the bundled catalog, defaulting
to the entries the catalog now flags `defaultEnabled` (OpenHands/extensions#485).
`disabled_skills` keeps its job for user- and project-authored skills, which are
discovered at runtime and should be on the moment they appear.

`undefined` is the "never migrated" sentinel, so it is deliberately kept out of
`DEFAULT_SETTINGS` and out of the `use-settings` coercions. A one-shot migration
at the app root converts each workspace once: one that had switched catalog
skills off keeps everything else on, a fresh one gets the curated default, and
both persist an explicit list so a later `defaultEnabled` addition cannot switch
itself on. It skips cloud, which creates conversations from its own server-side
catalog and never reads the field.","html_url":"https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/commit/b28af79ef06f6aedb449b56888ebe9b727c48939"},{"sha":"0a76cb9b97e45f3abfbaa6c5b893e7baac89f250","message":"feat(skills): surface the allow-list in Customize

Both skill surfaces — the Customize page and the conversation drawer — held
their own copy of the hydrate / auto-save / toggle logic against
`disabled_skills`. The two lists behind enablement are not symmetric, so a
shared `useSkillEnablement` hook now owns the decision of which list a given
skill belongs to: leaving it in two places would let one surface write a
preference the other cannot see. Re-enabling a catalog skill also drops it from
an unmigrated deny-list, where a stale entry would otherwise veto it.

Cards carry a "Recommended" badge for the catalog's `defaultEnabled` entries,
and a matching facet filters by it. The facet hides itself when nothing
discriminates, which is what keeps it off cloud, where the allow-list does not
apply and toggles stay on the deny-list.

The filter helpers now take enablement as a predicate rather than a deny-set:
resolving two lists is the caller's concern, not the filter's.

A notice on the page states that changes reach new conversations only.","html_url":"https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/commit/0a76cb9b97e45f3abfbaa6c5b893e7baac89f250"},{"sha":"e5c848586bed65324d126314691f661e185b5139","message":"docs(skills): add PR screenshots for the skill allow-list","html_url":"https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/commit/e5c848586bed65324d126314691f661e185b5139"},{"sha":"8b8b31b8b7465b4a790f487d2bf956f259db8c37","message":"fix(skills): load a catalog skill the opening slash command invokes

The allow-list broke automation presets, caught by the mock-LLM E2E
`preset automation → slash command conversation` spec: the conversation came
back with `activated_skills=[]`.

An automation card fills the chat input with its skill's own command — the
first entry of the skill's `triggers`, via `findAutomationCommand` — and 18 of
the catalog's 24 slash commands belong to skills that are off by default. So
the command reached the agent as a bare string with none of the instructions
behind it, and the card looked like it did nothing.

Naming a command is a stronger signal than either stored list, so an invoked
skill is loaded for that conversation whatever the lists say, and without
changing them. Only the leading token counts: matching a `/word` anywhere in
prose would re-admit most of the catalog through the back door, which is the
behaviour the allow-list exists to remove. `/<skill-name>` is indexed too,
since that is what the detail modal's "Use skill" button inserts.","html_url":"https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/commit/8b8b31b8b7465b4a790f487d2bf956f259db8c37"},{"sha":"304d02c5d4a6a808296cb974bb99f2fe23bc8b7d","message":"refactor(skills): share one enablement rule and trim the commentary

`isSkillEnabled` was dead in production while `useSkillEnablement` re-implemented
it, so the rule lived in two places. Both callers now build it once through
`buildSkillEnablementFilter`, which also keeps the per-skill check off the
resolve path in the Customize render loop.

Fixes a race the split introduced: the toggle surfaces persisted their hydrated
state on mount, which for an unmigrated workspace wrote the curated default and
could land after — and so undo — the migration that had just preserved the
workspace's own set. The save now runs only when the lists actually change,
which also drops a redundant PATCH per page visit.

`CATALOG_SKILL_NAMES` and `RECOMMENDED_SKILL_NAMES` were exported but unused
outside their module; the first is now what the cloud branch hydrates from and
the second is private. `findInvokedCatalogSkills` returned an array that could
only ever hold one entry, so it is singular. Both toggle surfaces called
`setEnabled` through a wrapper that added nothing.","html_url":"https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/commit/304d02c5d4a6a808296cb974bb99f2fe23bc8b7d"},{"sha":"fae6ad8a0ccaaa5ec8f87aac36abe321e72fbb2c","message":"fix(skills): list only enabled skills in the conversation Skills modal

"Show Available Skills" read the raw catalog and filtered nothing, so it
reported all 59 bundled skills as available while the agent had 11. The claim
was already loose before the allow-list — a skill on the deny-list still
appeared — but going from a handful of exceptions to 48 makes it wrong.

The modal is read-only, so it takes the same rule through a new
`useSkillEnabledFilter` rather than the toggle hook, and the settings-to-lists
mapping (including the cloud carve-out) is now shared by both.

The slash-command menu deliberately keeps listing every command: invoking one
by name loads its skill for that conversation.","html_url":"https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/commit/fae6ad8a0ccaaa5ec8f87aac36abe321e72fbb2c"}]

Of 59 skills only the 11 render enabled; add-javadoc and bitbucket — the skills from #16302 — start disabled. disabled_skills still governs user/project skills from .agents/skills/.

Upstream PR report: npx vitest run yields 5064 passed with one unrelated pre-existing failure (dev-with-automation SIGHUP cleanup, failing identically on main); lint and translation-completeness checks are clean, with the 4 new keys translated for all 15 locales.

The adapter tests flipped to assert add-javadoc is absent from agent context — that flip is the fix.

Remaining uncertainty, per the PR: per-workspace scoping needs an SDK WorkspacesClient schema change; cloud is untouched (server-side catalog); and the agent-profile disabled_skills deny-list is a second, independent list the adapter never consults, so which wins is unresolved. I personally ran no tests; Vitest, lint, and translation results are attributed to the PR report.

## Findings on OpenHands/OpenHands #16860 (public GitHub evidence)

**1. The allow-list change.** PR #16860 replaces the all-on skill catalog with `enabled_skills`, an allow-list over the bundled `@openhands/extensions` catalog, defaulting to the 11 entries the catalog flags `defaultEnabled` (Phase 0 shipped in extensions#485; the repo pins 0.18.0). Of 59 skills only the 11 render enabled; `add-javadoc` and `bitbucket` — the skills from #16302 — start disabled. `disabled_skills` still governs user/project skills from `.agents/skills/`.

**2. Two key implementation files.** The decision point is `src/utils/skill-enablement.ts`: `buildSkillEnablementFilter`, one-shot `migrateSkillEnablement`, and `findInvokedCatalogSkill` (a leading slash command loads that skill regardless of the lists). `src/hooks/use-skill-enablement.ts` is the shared toggle hook replacing duplicate hydrate/auto-save logic in Customize and the conversation drawer, so one surface can't write a preference the other can't see.

**3. The test runner.** Upstream PR report: `npx vitest run` yields 5064 passed with one unrelated pre-existing failure (`dev-with-automation` SIGHUP cleanup, failing identically on `main`); lint and translation-completeness checks are clean, with the 4 new keys translated for all 15 locales.

**4. New test files.** `__tests__/utils/skill-enablement.test.ts` (resolve, deny-veto, every migration branch) and `__tests__/hooks/use-migrate-enabled-skills.test.tsx` (one-shot, cloud skip, no write over a failed settings load), plus route and facet cases. The adapter tests flipped to assert `add-javadoc` is absent from agent context — that flip is the fix.

**5. Remaining uncertainty (per the PR).** Per-workspace scoping needs an SDK `WorkspacesClient` schema change; cloud is untouched (server-side catalog); and the agent-profile `disabled_skills` deny-list is a second, independent list the adapter never consults, so which wins is unresolved. **I personally ran no tests;** the Vitest, lint, and translation results are attributed to the upstream PR report.
